call_points.text: Management expects double-digit growth to continue for the next 5-10 years, calling last year's weather-hit low base an exception.
India capex guided at under ₹500-600 Cr this year, with most probably only one new plant.
Enough capacity to handle 50% volume growth without adding any capacity.
Targeting close to half a million new outlets this year on a base of about 4 million.
Raw material stocked for two quarters; international impact from higher oil prices seen as practically zero to a couple of points.
India raw material covered for this quarter, partly for next; discounts being cut to offset cost inflation.
New plant payback normally 3-4 years with 30% RoCE.
Transportation cost is the only input that cannot be stocked; management says it can absorb the impact.
Aluminium can shortage affects the industry; cans are less than 2% of VBL sales and it has tied up enough supply.

guidance.statement: Double-digit growth expected for the next 5-10 years
India capex under ₹500-600 Cr this year
Add close to half a million outlets this year
Management expects to keep growing at 20% plus in most markets, and sees no reason not to grow in double digits in India
Margins can be comfortably maintained even in a worst-case geopolitical year

operating_notes.text: Twizza Proprietary Limited acquired as a 100% step-down subsidiary in South Africa effective March 18, 2026.
Q1 CY2026 consolidated sales volume 363.4 million cases, up 16.3% YoY; India volumes +14.4%, international +21.4%.
Low sugar / No sugar products rose to ~63% of consolidated sales volumes in Q1 CY2026.
India contributed ~67% of revenues from operations (net) in Fiscal 2025.
Q1 CY2026 consolidated sales volume 363.4 million cases, up 16.3% YoY; India +14.4%, international +21.4%.
CSD 73.6% of volumes, non-carbonated 7.5%, packaged water 18.9%; low/no sugar ~63% of volumes.
Snack foods revenue in Q1 CY2026 was ₹112 Cr vs ₹52 Cr last year.
Revised PepsiCo EBA for India runs up to April 30, 2049 (earlier April 30, 2039); the SPV-only restriction on VBL is deleted.
Low-sugar and no-sugar products contributed about 73% of consolidated volume in H1 CY2026.
Cans are only 1-2% of the business and were the minor supply issue in April.
Food distribution and manufacturing in Africa is growing at about 50%.

timeline.summary: Varun Beverages Limited will host a conference call for investors and analysts on April 27, 2026, at 2:30 PM IST to discuss Q1 CY 2026 results, led by senior management.
On April 22, 2026, Varun Beverages informed the exchange about issuing a corporate guarantee of ZAR 770 million for its South African subsidiary Bevco.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹6,721.54 Cr (+18.3% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹872.36 Cr (+20.1% YoY).
Q1 CY2026 results (consolidated): revenue ₹6,574 Cr (+18.1% YoY), EBITDA ₹1,529 Cr (+21.0%), PAT ₹879 Cr (+20.1%); board approved interim dividend of ₹0.50 per share.
Varun Beverages Limited shared the audio recording of its Investors & Analysts Conference Call on April 27, 2026, following Q1 CY2026 unaudited results.

Varun Beverages' Q1 CY2026 earnings call (April 27, 2026) guided India capex under ₹500-600 Cr for the year, said it has capacity for 50% volume growth without additions, and reiterated double-digit growth for 5-10 years.
Varun Beverages Ltd. will participate in an investor meeting on May 19, 2026, in Singapore with Mr. Raj Gandhi and Mr. Deepak Dabas.

On May 21, 2026, Varun Beverages and PepsiCo signed a revised Exclusive Bottling Appointment and Trademark License Agreement for India, extending the term to April 30, 2049 from April 30, 2039 and deleting the clause restricting VBL to an SPV role for PepsiCo business.

Varun Beverages’ **Mr. Raj Gandhi** and **Mr. Deepak Dabas** will attend investor meetings at BofA India Conference (June 3), Morgan Stanley India Investment Forum (June 3), and Citi India Conference (June 4) in Mumbai.

watchlist.text: Regulatory and other approvals for Crickley Dairy acquisition

watchlist.response: Well-stocked for two quarters; will cut discounts and costs to protect bottom line.
watchlist.text: Impact of higher oil prices on packaging and transportation costs

watchlist.response: Gave revenue (~₹800 Cr and ~₹160 Cr) but said margins are 'a bit too early' to guide.
watchlist.text: Revenue and margin run-rate for Twizza and Crickley Dairy

watchlist.response: Said it is difficult to answer but believes others will blink first; does not see itself taking a hit.
watchlist.text: Whether margins can be held if crude stays at $100 for several quarters

watchlist.response: Ravi Jaipuria said the quarter should not be looked at alone, July is looking very good, and growth should be judged yearly; Varun Jaipuria attributed the softness to the El Nino effect on May seasonality.
watchlist.text: Percy Panthaki noted India growth looks strong only on a favourable base, with 2-year CAGR of about 3% and 3-year CAGR in single digits

watchlist.response: Management said volumes are tracked on an 8-ounce basis and that realisation and gross margin per 8-ounce case have not fallen, calling the pack change immaterial.
watchlist.text: Abneesh Roy asked how much of volume growth comes from larger pack grammage versus real consumption

watchlist.response: Ravi Jaipuria declined, saying the question should be put to PepsiCo and that VBL does not go into market share.
watchlist.text: Jay Doshi asked what data PepsiCo uses for its India market-share comment

watchlist.response: Varun Jaipuria said specifics could not be given, but new categories are growing 3x-4x the overall business; Ravi Jaipuria later said VAD is growing over 40% and Nimbooz more than 30%.
watchlist.text: Aditya Soman asked for category-wise growth for new launches
